47-1300000001.title: CERTIFIED PUBLIC ACCOUNTANT (CPA)
47-1300000001.description:
CERTIFIED PUBLIC ACCOUNTANT (CPA)

CERTIFICATION REQUIREMENTS:
To become a CPA in Tennessee, candidates must obtain 150 semester hours of education and must earn a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university. This must include 30 semester hours in accounting (24 of which must be in upper division courses) and 24 semester hours in business courses (12 of which must be in upper division courses). The candidate must then pass the Uniform CPA Examination, pass an ethics examination given by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA) with a score of 90% or better, and complete one year of experience in accounting acceptable to the Board.

Once both exams have been passed, the Board is notified and an application packet is sent to the candidate to apply for the Tennessee CPA certificate. The CPA applicant must have completed the TNSBA experience requirement prior to submitting an application for certification.

EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS
The experience requirements as outlined in T.C.A. Section 62-1-106(j) include:

 Employment in industry, government, academia or public practice

47-1300000003.title: LICENSED PUBLIC ACCOUNTANT
47-1300000003.description:
LICENSED PUBLIC ACCOUNTANT

Licensed Public Accountant (LPA) - an individual admitted to practice public accounting by their state board of Accountancy.
REQUIREMENTS: Uniform CPA Examination passing grades. AICPA Ethics Examination passing grade. Experience may consist of providing any type of services or advice using accounting, attest, management advisory, financial advisory, tax or consulting skills. Acceptable experience shall include employment in industry, government, academia or public practice. No fewer than 2,000 hours of experience (earned in no less than one year or more than three years). Experience must be earned within the ten (10) years immediately preceding the application for certification.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS: Must earn a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university and obtain a total of 150 semester hours of education. Education must include 30 semester hours in accounting (24 of which must be in upper division courses) and 24 semester hours in business courses.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
Candidates must get a score of 75 in order to pass the Certified Public Accountant (CPA) Exam. Score 90 or more to pass the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA) Ethics Examination.

47-1700000003.description:
PROFESSIONAL ENGINEER

Engineers use the knowledge of mathematical and natural sciences to develop ways to utilize the materials and forces of nature for the benefit of humankind. Engineers practice in a wide range of disciplines, from traditional disciplines like civil, mechanical, and electrical, to more specialized disciplines like nuclear and industrial.
Applicants for registration must complete:

47-1900000009.description:
PROFESSIONAL SOIL SCIENTIST

Licensed professional soil scientist means a person who is licensed as a soil scientist under the provisions of this part. Soil scientist means a person qualified by education and practical experience to engage in the practice of soil science.

REQUIREMENTS:
To be eligible for a certificate of licensure, an applicant shall meet each of the following minimum qualifications:

(2) Have at least three (3) years of soil science professional experience. Any combination of the following kinds of education and experience qualify toward accumulating the required three (3) years:
(A) Masters of science degree in soils, agronomy or a closely related field and two (2) years of professional experience;

00-18.title: Air Traffic Control Tower Operator
00-18.description: Requirements to obtain an Air Traffic Control Tower Operator certificate include passing a written test. Besides the basic certificate, to act at any operating position, the individual must pass a practical test on control tower equipment and its use. To obtain a facility rating, the individual must have at least six months experience and pass another practical test. This certificate is valid until surrendered, suspended or revoked, although the individual must maintain current experience to work under the certificate. Detailed information can be found at web sites:http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ, http://www.natca.org/assets/Documents/mediacenter/controller_brochure.pdf, http://www2.faa.gov/careers/employment/atc.htm, and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.31-65.50.

00-12.title: Aircraft Mechanic - A & P
00-12.description: Aircraft mechanics are certified by the FAA with either an airframe (A) or powerplant (P) rating. Initial ratings require either completion of FAA Approved Aviation Maintenance Technician School or 18 months of work experience. Applicants must pass written, oral and practical exams. Thirty months of work experience is required for a combined Airframe & Powerplant (A & P) certificate. To obtain an inspector's authorization, a mechanic must have held an A & P certificate for at least 3 years. This certificate is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked, but requires currency of experience or refresher training. For further information, go the web site of the Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS): http://umet-vets.dol.gov/airframe-mechanic.htm, http://www1.faa.gov/AVR/afs/mechanics.htm, and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.71-65.95.

00-16.title: Aircraft Repairer
00-16.description: To be eligible for a repairman certificate, a person must have the qualifications needed on the job. These qualifications may be obtained through 18 months of work experience or completion of formal training. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www2.faa.gov/education/rlib/career.htm and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.101-65.105.

00-02.title: Airline Transport Pilot
00-02.description: To become certified (licensed) as an Airline Transport Pilot (ATP), an individual must have a Commercial Pilot certificate or equivalent with an instrument rating for airplane, helicopter, or powered-lift (glider). Air flight training and ground school as well as flight experience are requirements. They also must pass a strict physical examination and have 20/20 vision with or without glasses, good hearing, and no physical handicaps that could impair performance. They must pass a written test and a demonstration of flying ability. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.151-61.167.

00-08.title: Commercial Pilot
00-08.description: All pilots who are paid to transport passengers or cargo must have a Commercial Pilot's license with an instrument rating issued by the FAA. To qualify for this license, the applicant must be at least 18 years old and have at least 250 hours of flight experience. The time can be reduced through participation in certain flight school curricula approved by the FAA. The individual also must pass a strict physical examination and have 20/20 vision with or without glasses, good hearing, and no physical handicaps that could impair performance. Passing a written test and a demonstration of flying ability are required. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.121-61.133 and http://www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf.

00-15.title: Flight Engineer
00-15.description: To become certified as a Flight Engineer requires that the individual have either training or experience. Passing a written exam and a practical test and having a current medical certificate are also required. This certificate is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://umet-vets.dol.gov/flightengineer.htm and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr63_00.html, parts 63.31-63.43.

00-77.title: Flight Instructor
00-77.description: To obtain certification as a Flight Instructor, the individual must hold either a Commercial Pilot or Airline Transport Pilot certificate with appropriate aircraft and instrument ratings. Training is required as well as experience in the type of aircraft being rated. This license is valid for 2 years and may be renewed by one of several options, such as passing a practical test, documenting student success, or taking a refresher course. More details can be found at web sites: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.181-61.199, www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf, and http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ.

00-20.title: Flight Navigator
00-20.description: To become certified as a Flight Navigator, the individual must be at least 21 years old and have a medical certificate. He or she must have both training in flight navigation and practical experience. Passing written and practical tests are required as well as having a current medical certificate. This certificate is valid until surrendered, suspended, or revoked. Detailed information can be found on the web site: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr63_00.html, parts 63.51-63.61.

00-13.title: Ground Instructor
00-13.description: To obtain certification as a Ground Instructor, the individual must pass an aircraft navigation knowledge test and a test of the fundamentals of instructing, unless the person already is employed as a teacher or holds a teacher's certification. Detailed information can be found at web sites: http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.211-61.217.

00-06.title: Private Pilot
00-06.description: Obtaining a Private Pilot certificate (license) requires the individual to complete ground and flight training, have flight experience, obtain a medical certificate, and pass a written exam as well as a demonstration of flying ability. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. The applicant must hold a post- high school degree from an accredited university, college, or technical college approved by the commissioner; or hold a current certification by a national training program approved by the commissioner in the field of work to be installed, serviced, or monitored and have at least three years of working experience in the alarm industry covering the actual installation of alarm systems.

MEDICAL DOCTORS

47-1700000002.description:
PROFESSIONAL ARCHITECT

An architect initiates and develops conceptual designs and details for the construction of new buildings and the renovation or repairs of existing buildings. An architect is responsible for the technical preparation of construction documents. The person with this job title provides overall project direction, including coordination with other disciplines involved in the project. To use the title architect in Tennessee, a person must be registered with the registering authority. There are limited circumstances under which individuals may perform architectural work without being registered, as long as they do not call themselves architects. However, there are other circumstances, delineated in Tennessee law, which require a registered architect.

REQUIREMENTS:
Must be able to speak and write the English language, be of good character and repute, and complete the education, experience, and examination requirements.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:
Graduation from a school of architecture whose curriculum has been accredited plus completion of three years of practical experience in architectural work satisfactory to the board. Other combinations of education and experience may be accepted by the state board, as specified in Tennessee law.

00-48.title: Second Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-48.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Second Assistant Engineer - Upper Level, the applicant must, while holding a license as a Third Assistant Engineer, complete one of the following: 360 days of service as an Assistant Engineer; or a minimum of 180 days as an Assistant Engineer and 360 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED); or 360 days as Chief Engineer (Limited-Oceans). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.

Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Detailed information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.

Boxing participants are required to pay a licensing fee of $100 for managers, $25 for boxing seconds, and $100 for matchmakers. An additional $50 fee is required for application. States or localities where a license has been held and the length those licenses have been active must be included in the application paperwork.

47-2700000001.title: ATHLETIC TRAINER
47-2700000001.description:
ATHLETIC TRAINER

Athletic trainers provide medical management, prevention, and treatment of athletic injuries. They design training programs, treat and rehabilitate injuries under the direction of a physician or therapist and use knowledge of nutrition, conditioning, protective equipment and psychology to help athletic performance.

REQUIREMENTS:
Satisfy education and experience requirements and examination requirements.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS:
The applicant must have received a baccalaureate degree, have obtained at least 1,500 hours of supervised athletic training experience and successfully completed at least one formal course in each of the following areas: health, human anatomy, kinesiology/biomechanics, human physiology, physiology of exercise, basic athletic training, and advanced athletic training.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
Administered four (4) times a year.

RENEWAL REQUIREMENTS:
Every two years.

47-2900000005.title: AUDIOLOGISTS
47-2900000005.description:
AUDIOLOGISTS

Audiology is the application of non-medical principles, methods and procedures for the assessment of auditory vestibular systems, including the interpretation of behavioral and physiologic measures, and the design and implementation of programs of hearing conservation and preservation and programs of habilitation and rehabilitation for auditory and vestibular disorders. This includes the assessment, selection, fitting and sale of amplification systems or other assistive devices and technologies; and the testing, appraisal, prediction, consultation, counseling, and instruction related to hearing and disorders of hearing. An audiologist will check hearing for the purpose of modifying communicative disorders involving speech, language, auditory functions, or other aberrant behavior related to hearing loss.

REQUIREMENTS:
Be at least 18 years of age of good moral character and satisfy education and examination requirements.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Four year program plus clinical experience, and a Doctoral Degree in the area of audiology.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
ASHA certified or has taken the Praxis examination in audiology with a minimum score of 170 administered by Education Testing Service, Princeton, New Jersey 08541.

CONTINUING EDUCATION:
A minimum of ten hours per year approved by the board.

47-4100000004.description:
AUTOMOBILE CLUB OR AUTOMOBILE ASSOCIATION AGENT

a n individual is required to be licensed under the laws of this state to sell, solicit or negotiate membership in an automobile club or association/

LICENSE REQUIREMENTS:

00-65.description: The Ship Radar Endorsement is issued by the Federal Communications Commission to licensed commercial radio operators. This endorsement allows them to repair, maintain, or internally adjust ship radar equipment. Passing a written exam is required. For further information, see the FCC web site at http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/sre.html.

47-3900000003.title: BARBER TECHNICIAN
47-3900000003.description:
BARBER TECHNICIAN

Applies tints or dyes to the hair, shampoos hair, manicures nails, applies cosmetic preparations, antiseptics, powders, oils, clays or lotions to scalp, face, neck or other parts of the body.

REQUIREMENTS:
Be at least seventeen years of age, not owe any money to a barbering school, and meet education and examination requirements.

EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
A tenth grade education and satisfactory completion of a course in a registered barber school or college of not less than 340 hours of continuous instruction of not more than 8 hours per day and 40 hours per week.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
The board conducts examinations not less than four times each year.
47-3900000003.agency: Department of Commerce and Insurance · Division of Regulatory Boards · Division of Regulatory Boards

47-3900000008.title: MASTER BARBER
47-3900000008.description:
MASTER BARBER

A barber performs one or any combination of practices listed for payment, directly or indirectly, or without payment for the public generally: shaving or trimming beards, cutting or styling the hair, giving facial and scalp massages or treatments with oils, creams, lotions or other preparations either by hand or mechanical appliances; singeing, curling, shampooing, coloring, bleaching or straightening the hair, or applying hair tonics; cutting, fitting, measuring and forming head caps for wigs or hair pieces; hair weaving (excluding medical or surgical procedures); applying cosmetic preparations, antiseptics, powders, oils, clays or lotions to scalp, face, neck or other parts of the body; or manicuring and nail care. (A technician's license is available that permits a limited number of the above practices.)

REQUIREMENTS:
Be at least seventeen years of age, not owing any money to the barbering school, and satisfying education and examination requirements.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Tenth-grade education or equivalent and satisfactory completion of fifteen hundred (1,500) hours in a registered barber school. 750 hours of approved training in a registered school of cosmetology can count towards the 1,500 required hours in the registered barber school.

RENEWAL REQUIREMENTS:
Renewal required every two years.
47-3900000008.agency: Department of Commerce and Insurance · Division of Regulatory Boards · Division of Regulatory Boards

47-3900000001.title: MASTER BARBER INSTRUCTOR
47-3900000001.description:
MASTER BARBER INSTRUCTOR

A registered master barber certified by the board as a barber instructor.

PROSPECTIVE:
No barber school or college may operate without the presence of a registered barber instructor. A barber school must have at least one registered barber instructor or barber instructor assistant for every 15 students enrolled, and must have one licensed barber instructor for each barber instruction assistant.

REQUIREMENTS:
Holds a valid license to instruct and completes 300 hours of training.
47-3900000001.agency: Department of Commerce and Insurance · Division of Regulatory Boards · Division of Regulatory Boards

47-3900000002.title: MASTER BARBER INSTRUCTOR'S ASSISTANT
47-3900000002.description:
MASTER BARBER INSTRUCTOR'S ASSISTANT

A registered master barber certified by the board as a barber instructor assistant. Employment as a barber instructor assistant is limited to three years.

PROSPECTIVE:
Every barber school must have one licensed barber instructor for each barber instructor assistant.

REQUIREMENTS:
Hold a valid certificate of registration as a master barber and meets the education and examination requirements.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Completion of tenth grade in an accredited school or equivalent, and current enrollment in a four hundred fifty-hour instructor training program at a board-certified barber school. Total Included with Masterbarber.

47-2700000014.title: TN BEAUTY PAGEANT OPERATOR
47-2700000014.description:
REGISTERED BEAUTY PAGEANT OPERATOR

Operate any contest or competition in which entrants are judged on the basis of physical beauty, skill, talent, poise, and personality, and in which a winner, or winners, are selected as representing an ideal in one or more areas. It excludes contests in which no application fee is charged for contestants.

Register with the Consumer Affairs Division of the Department of Commerce and Insurance and post a $10,000 surety bond.

Annual.

47-3900000004.title: COSMETOLOGIST
47-3900000004.description:
COSMETOLOGIST

A cosmetologist performs, for compensation, arranging, dressing, curling, waving, cleansing, cutting, singeing, bleaching, coloring, or similar work on the hair. A cosmetologist may care for or service wigs or hair pieces; manicure; massage, clean, stimulate, manipulate, exercise, beautify or perform similar work upon the hands, arms, face neck or feet with hands or by use of cosmetic preparations, tonics, lotions or creams; place or apply artificial eyelashes, give facials, apply makeup, give skin care, or remove superfluous hair by tweezing, depilatories, or waxing.

REQUIREMENTS:
Be at least 16 years of age and meet educational and examination requirements.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Completion of 1,500 hours in practice and theory at a school of cosmetology.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
Written and practical national examination.

RENEWAL REQUIREMENTS:
Renewal notices mailed approximately one month prior to renewal date. Licensee required to submit renewal notice with required fee, if applicable, due by expiration date on license.

CONTINUING EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
Twenty-four (24) hours every two years for cosmetology instructors.

PROFESSIONAL ORGANIZATIONS:
Tennessee Cosmetology Association

47-2500000001.title: COSMETOLOGY INSTRUCTOR
47-2500000001.description:
COSMETOLOGY INSTRUCTOR

This is a person who is licensed as a cosmetologist and is certified with the board as a cosmetology instructor. The person may not practice cosmetology as a profession within a school setting, but may practice as a cosmetologist elsewhere.

PROSPECTIVE:
A school of cosmetology must have at least one certified instructor, and must have at least one certified instructor for each junior instructor. A certified instructor must be on the premises whenever a cosmetology school (including public high school or state vocational technical school offering cosmetology courses) is in operation.

REQUIREMENTS:
Hold a valid license cosmetologist's, manicurist's , aesthetician's, or natural hair stylist's license issued by the board; and meet educational and experience requirements.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS:
Be a high school graduate or possess a graduate equivalency diploma (G.E.D) AND EITHER Complete a board-approved course in instructor training of at least 300 hours within a period of six months as an instructor trainee OR Complete service as a junior instructor for a minimum of one year.

EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENT:
Has been licensed as a cosmetologist, aesthetician, manicurist, or natural hair stylist for at least three continuous years.

47-3900000005.title: ELECTROLOGIST
47-3900000005.description:
ELECTROLOGIST

An electrologist removes hair from the normal skin of the human body by application of an electric current to the hair papilla by means of a needle or needles so as to cause growth inactivity of the hair papilla and thus permanently remove the hair.

REQUIREMENTS:
Be at least 18 years of age, with good moral character, and satisfy the education and examination requirements.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
A high school diploma or equivalent and 600 hours electrology (175 theory and 425 clinical practice); completed within a twelve (12) month time frame from the date started, and must have been completed prior to taking the examination.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
The written examination, as adopted by the Commissioner, is the examination accepted by the American Electrology Association (AEA) or Society for Clinical and Medical Hair Removal, Inc. (SCMHR)

RENEWAL REQUIREMENTS:
Every two (2) years.

47-3900000014.title: HAIR BRAIDER
47-3900000014.description:
HAIR BRAIDER: A person that uses techniques that result in tension on hair strands, such as twisting, wrapping, weaving, extending, locking, or braiding of the hair, by hand or mechanical appliances for compensation, without cutting, coloring, relaxing, removing, chemically treating, or using other preparations to straighten, curl, or alter the structure of the hair.

REQUIREMENTS: Effective July 1, 2019, hair braiders are exempt from licensure (Title 62, Chapter 4) provided that the general requirements and educational requirements are met including: Using only disposable or properly sanitized instruments. Workers must be at least 14 years of age, according to state labor law. Post a notice that the hair braider is not licensed. A person providing hair braiding services pursuant to this section shall not refer to themselves as a licensed natural hair stylist unless the person otherwise meets the requirements under TCA§ 62-4-ll0(f).

47-2900000009.title: CYTOTECHNOLOGIST
47-2900000009.description:
CYTOTECHNOLOGIST

A cytotechnologist (CT) is a laboratory professional who uses special techniques to study the function and structure of human cells. Changes caused by disease such as cancer can be detected by CTs, who prepare slides of cell samples, examine cell samples with a microscope and detect abnormal hormone conditions. The cytotechnologist is responsible for documenting the slide interpretation results of each gynecologic and nongynecologic cytology test examined or reviewed. (A license is required for each person examining cytology slide preparations.

REQUIREMENTS:
Be certified in cytotechnology by a certifying agency approved by the board and meet educational requirements. (Less stringent requirements may apply to renewal for those licensed before August 1, 1988.)

EDUCATION:
Graduation from a school of cytotechnology accredited by the Committee on Accreditation of Allied Health Education Programs (CAAHEP) or other accediting agency acceptable to the Board.

NATIONAL CERTIFICATION:
(CT) Cytotechnologist American Society for Clinical Pathologist (ASCP) Board of Certification.

RENEWALS:
Licenses must be renewed every two years.

47-2900000023.title: MEDICAL LABORATORY TECHNICIAN
47-2900000023.description:
MEDICAL LABORATORY TECHNICIAN

A medical laboratory technician is any person other than the medical laboratory director, supervisor, technologist or trainee who functions under the supervision of a medical laboratory director, supervisor or technologist and performs only those medical laboratory procedures which require limited skill, responsibility, and minimal independent judgement.

REQUIREMENTS:
A medical laboratory technician must possess an associate's degree in a medical laboratory technician training program which has a National Accrediting Agency for Clinical Laboratory Science (NAACLS) approved training program, an Associate's degree with 6 semester hours of chemistry, 6 semester hours of biology and three (3) years of full time clinical work experience or an Associate's degree in laboratory science and successful completion of an official military laboratory procedures course of at least fifty (50) weeks duration in residence and have held the military enlisted occupational specialty of Medical Laboratory Specialist (Medical Laboratory Technician) reference on Form DD214, a copy of which must be included, in addition to possessing national certification by examination.

Performs tests requiring independent judgment and responsibility with minimal supervision in specialties or subspecialties for which qualified, may be limited to one specialty.

National certification by exam, required education, NAACLS approved training program or experience.

00-21.title: FIRST Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T1
00-21.description: FIRST Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T1) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. Further information can be found at the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-24.title: General Radiotelephone Operator License - PG
00-24.description: General Radiotelephone Operator License (PG) is issued for a lifetime and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-26.title: GMDSS Radio Maintainer's License - DM
00-26.description: GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) Radio Maintainer's License (DM) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-27.title: GMDSS Radio Operator's License - DO
00-27.description: GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) Radio Operator's License (DO) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-25.title: Marine Radio Operator Permit - MP
00-25.description: Marine Radio Operator Permit (MP) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-58.title: Radio Officer
00-58.description: The Radio Officer's license is issued to applicants who have a valid Federal Communications Commission (FCC) license as first or second class radiotelegraph operator (T1, T2). Certain officers are required to hold Global Maritime Distress and Safety System (GMDSS) certification issued by the FCC. Further information can be found at theUSCG website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-58.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-75.title: Restricted Radiotelephone Operator Permit (RP)
00-75.description: RP holders are authorized to operate most aircraft and aeronautical ground stations. They can also operate marine radiotelephone stations aboard pleasure craft (other than those carrying more than six passengers for hire on the Great Lakes or bays or tidewaters or in the open sea) when operator licensing is required. To obtain this permit, you must be able to speak and hear; and keep a written log; and be familiar with provisions of applicable treaties, laws and rules which govern the radio station you will operate. For further information, see the Federal Communications web site at http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/rp.html.

00-22.title: SECOND Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T2
00-22.description: SECOND Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T2) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-23.title: THIRD Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T3
00-23.description: THIRD Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T3) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-57.title: Assistant Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels
00-57.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as an Assistant Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels include 1,080 days at sea with 720 days on Motor Vessels. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-57.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-56.title: Chief Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels
00-56.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels include 1,440 days at sea with 360 days as a Licensed Engineer and 950 days on Motor Vessels. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm.
00-56.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-19.title: Inspector's Authorization
00-19.description: To obtain an inspector's authorization, a mechanic must have held an Aircraft Mechanic A & P certificate for at least 3 years. For further information, see web site http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ, parts 65.91-65.95.

00-41.title: Operator of Uninspected Passenger Vessels - OUPV
00-41.description: To become licensed as an Operator of Uninspected Passenger Vessels requires specific experience -- Near Coastal or Inland as well as passing a written exam. Recent training in First Aid and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is also required. For complete details see the USCG web page http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr13_02, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at website http://frwebgate4.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/waisgate.cgi?WAISdocID=50846230377+3+0+0&WAISaction=retrieve or http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.

00-42.title: Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels - OUTV
00-42.description: To become licensed as a an Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels (OUTV) or 2nd Class Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels (OUTV) requires specific experience - Oceans (Domestic Route), Near Coastal or Inland, as well as passing a written exam. Recent training in First Aid and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is also required. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Details can be found on the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.

47-5100000002.title: BOILER INSPECTOR
47-5100000002.description:
BOILER INSPECTOR

A boiler inspector is commissioned by the state to inspect power boilers, low pressure heating boilers, and unfired pressure vessels as to construction, installation, condition and function before regular operation and periodically before certificates expire, and to certify the satisfactory inspection and the maximum pressure under which the boiler may be operated.
[The inspector is a state employee, an employee of an insurer of boilers in the state, or an employee of a company with an approved inspection program for boilers it owns or uses.]

PROSPECTIVE:
A certificate of competency is required for appointment as chief inspector, assistant chief, deputy inspector, or special inspector in Tennessee.

REQUIREMENTS:
A commission or user-owner commission (as applicable) issued by the National Board of Boiler and Pressure Vessel Inspectors. Education and experience requirements below must be met to sit for the examination.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS:
A degree from an accredited school in mechanical engineering, plus one year of experience in design, construction, operation or inspection of high-pressure boilers and pressure vessels

47-5100000020.title: CERTIFIED ELECTRICAL INSPECTORS
47-5100000020.description:
CERTIFIED ELECTRICAL INSPECTORS

Inspect residential and commercial buildings for adherence to electrical codes.

EDUCATION:
Successfully complete a recognized and accepted training course provided by professional building codes organizations identified in Tenn. Comp. R. & Regs. 0780-02-16-.04

EXAMINATION AND CERTIFICATION:
Certification from the following professional building codes organizations provides the appropriate level of standards and qualifications necessary for certification: (a) International Code Council (ICC); (b) International Association of Electrical Inspectors (IAEI); (c) Other appropriate professional building code organizations recognized by the State Fire Marshal, or designee.Applicants must be U.S. citizens or qualified aliens. 36 hours, take examination, complete next level of certification.

47-4700000004.title: TENNESSEE HOME INSPECTOR LICENSING PROGRAM
47-4700000004.description:
TENNESSEE HOME INSPECTOR LICENSING PROGRAM

Home inspectors conduct inspections on residential properties to check for compliance and assess if there are hazards or structural defects. This entails examining both the interior and exterior of the property, including infrastructure, electrical and plumbing systems, and water quality.
REQUIREMENTS:

TN CERTIFIED INSPECTORS

Inspect residential and commercial buildings for adherence to fire, building, electrical, mechanical, and plumbing codes.

R. & Regs. 0780-02-16-.04, and/or an examination approved and recognized by the State Fire Marshal, or designee, which tests knowledge and skills in the specialty or specialties in which the applicant seeks certification.

47-2900000033.title: CLINICAL PERFUSIONIST
47-2900000033.description:
CLINICAL PERFUSIONIST

A clinical perfusionist operates special equipment that temporarily takes over a patient's respiratory and/or circulatory functions. This ensures that oxygen reaches the patient's body through the blood, even when the patient's lungs and heart are temporarily not functioning. They are part of the surgical team for operations such as open heart surgery.

EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
Graduation from an ACPE/CAHEA approved perfusion education program.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
Examinations are given by the American Board of Cardiovascular Perfusion or its successor organization.

RENEWAL REQUIREMENTS:
Every two (2) years before the last day of the month in which a license holder's birthday falls.

CONTINUING EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
Fifteen (15) hours of continuing education in courses approved by the Committee and Board every calendar year.

47-2900000007.title: CHIROPRACTIC PHYSICIAN
47-2900000007.description:
CHIROPRACTIC PHYSICIAN

A chiropractor manipulates the spinal column and adjacent tissues to prevent disease and correct abnormalities of the human body believed to be caused by interference with the nervous system.

REQUIREMENTS:
Be of good moral character, satisfy education and examination requirements.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Must have 60 hours from an accredited college or university and be a graduate from an accredited (CCE) Chiropractic College.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
The national exam parts I, II, III and physiotherapy are required; a written and practical examination are administered at the discretion of the board. (Part IV of the national examination is under consideration as an additional requirement.)

RENEWAL:
Renewal is required every two years

PROFESSIONAL ORGANIZATIONS:

47-1300000007.title: INSURANCE CROP ADJUSTER
47-1300000007.description:
INSURANCE CROP ADJUSTER

Any person, who, for compensation or any other thing of value, does any of the following:
 Acts or aids in investigating, verifying, substantiating, estimating, appraising, determining, presenting, and discussing the value of the claim, and/or effectuating the resolution of a claim for loss or damage covered by an insurance contract that insures crops;
 Advertises for employment as an adjuster of claims arising under the insurance contracts that insure crops or solicits business or represents to the public to be a crop insurance adjuster of insurance claims, for losses or damages arising out of policies of insurance that insure crops; or
 Directly or indirectly solicits business, investigates or adjusts losses, or advises an insured about claims for losses or damages arising out of policies or insurance that insure crops, when doing any of the forgoing for or on behalf of another person engaged in the business of adjusting losses or damages coved by an insurance policy that insures crops, for the insured.

LICENSE REQUIREMENTS:

47-4100000001.title: INSURANCE PRODUCER
47-4100000001.description:
INSURANCE PRODUCE

An individual is required to be licensed under the laws of this state to sell, solicit or negotiate a policy of insurance on an insurer's behalf. Insurance producer licenses are issued for the following lines of authority: Life, Accident & Health, Property, Casualty, Title and Personal Lines.

LICENSE REQUIREMENTS:
 Applicant must be 18 years of age
 Has not committed any act that is a ground for denial, suspension or revocation
 Complete 20 hours of pre-licensing education for each line of authority
NOTE: Pre-licensing and continuing education providers and courses must be approved by the Department of Commerce and Insurance for the licensing of insurance producers
 Pass state examination for the applicable line of authority
 Submit a finger-print based criminal background check
 Complete and file the NAIC uniform application and fee of $50.00

RENEWAL AND CONTINUING EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
 Completion of 24 hours of continuing education (including 3 hours ethics) is required biennially with the renewal of the license
 Licenses may be renewed for 2 years by submitting a completed NAIC uniform renewal application, fee and required continuing education

47-1300000010.title: PUBLIC ADJUSTER
47-1300000010.description:
PUBLIC ADJUSTER

Any person, other than someone who is employed by an insurance carrier, who, for compensation or any other thing of value, on behalf of the insured:

 Acts or aids, solely in relation to first party claims arising under insurance contracts that insure the real or personal property of the insured on behalf of an insured, in investigating, verifying, substantiating, estimating, appraising, determining, presenting, and discussing the value of the claim, and effectuating the resolution of a claim for loss or damage covered by an insurance contract;
 Advertises for employment as a public adjuster of insurance claims or solicits business or represents to the public to be a public adjuster of first party insurance claims, for losses or damages arising out of policies of insurance that insure real or personal property; or
 Directly or indirectly solicits business, investigates or adjusts losses, or advises an insured about first party claims for losses or damages arising out of policies of insurance that insure real or personal property for another person engaged in the business of adjusting losses or damages covered by an insurance policy, for the insured.

LICENSE REQUIREMENTS:

47-4100000018.title: SURPLUS LINES AGENT
47-4100000018.description:
SURPLUS LINES AGENT

An individual licensed as an insurance producer in Tennessee may be issued a surplus lines license granting the producer authority to procure the kinds of insurance from unauthorized companies in this stte under conditions prescribed in Tennessee Code Annotated  56-14-101 - 117.

REQUIREMENTS:
Applicant must hold a current insurance producer license in Tennessee. Complete and file the NAIC uniform application and fee of $120.00.

RENEWAL:
Licenses may be renewed for 2 years by submitting a completed NAIC uniform renewal application and fee.
47-4100000018.agency: Department of Commerce and Insurance · Insurance Division

47-4100000019.title: TITLE INSURANCE AGENT
47-4100000019.description:
TITLE INSURANCE AGENT

A title insurance agent has an agency contract or agreement with an insurance company to solicit or negotiate a policy of title insurance on the company's behalf.

REQUIREMENTS:
At least eighteen years of age; living or practicing in Tennessee; is competent, trustworthy and of good business reputation; and meets education and examination requirements as applicable.

EXPERIENCE:
Unless exempt from examination, must certify that the applicant has completed a prelicensing course of study of 5 hours approved by the commissioner.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
Pass an examination covering Tennessee laws and rules pertaining to insurance, general insurance terms, concepts, policy provisions, and contract law; as well as title insurance terms, concepts, and matters regarding the search and examination of title to real property. (Renewal applicants, applicants licensed in other states that offer the same privilege, and life applicants who earned the designation of chartered property and casualty underwriter are exempt from examination requirements.)

CONTINUING EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
At least 12 hours of study annually in approved courses, programs of instruction, or seminars during the twelve-month period immediately prior to renewal. A maximum of 12 additional hours of continuing education not needed to fulfill t…
47-4100000019.agency: Department of Commerce and Insurance · Insurance Division

47-5300000002.title: AERIAL APPLICATOR
47-5300000002.description:
AERIAL APPLICATOR

An aerial applicator engages in the application by aircraft of any substance or mixture of substances or chemicals intended for defoliating or desiccating plants, or for preventing, destroying, repelling, or mitigating any insects, rodents, fungi, bacteria, weeds or other forms of plant or animal life declared a pest by the Commissioner of Agriculture. An aerial applicators can use, buy or sell restricted pesticides only if licensed and certified by the Commissioner of Agriculture.

REQUIREMENTS:
Approval by the Commissioner of Agriculture as having the necessary technical qualifications and of the ability and intent to operate within applicable state and federal laws. Must have and adequate liability insurance coverage and satisfy examination requirements.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
Examinations are administered by the Department of Agriculture. Separate category examinations are required for certification to use, buy or sell restricted pesticides in a category. The examination must be taken every three years if the required number of continuing education units are not accrued to maintain the certification.

RENEWAL REQUIREMENTS:
Contact the licensing authority for information.

CONTINUING EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
Separate category examinations are required for certification to use, buy or sell restricted pes…
47-5300000002.agency: Department of Agriculture · Tennessee Pest Control Board

47-2300000002.title: COURT REPORTERS
47-2300000002.description:
COURT REPORTER

Court reporters make a verbatim record by means of manual shorthand, machine shorthand, closed microphone voice dictation silencer or by electronic recording of any testimony given under oath before or for submission to, any court, referee or court examiner, by any board, commission or other body or in any other proceeding where a verbatim record is required.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Satisfactory proof of graduation from a court reporting program or its equivalent.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
Proof of passage of the National Court Reporters Association registered professional reporter examination, the National Verbatim Reporters Association certified verbatim reporter examination, or the American Association of Electronic Reporters and Transcribers certified electronic court reporter examination.

CONTINUING EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
Twenty (20) hours or 2 continuing education credits.

RENEWAL:
Every two years
47-2300000002.agency: Department of Commerce and Insurance · Board of Court Reporting

47-2500000002.title: TEACHER
47-2500000002.description:
TEACHERS

Teachers instruct students in subject matter using various teaching methods including lecture and demonstration; use audiovisual aids and other materials to supplement presentations; prepare an outline for course work; assign lessons and correct homework; keep attendance records; and maintain discipline in the classroom. Teacher's license can be endorsed for many specialties, including elementary education, middle grades and secondary subject-specific endorsements, as well as many others.

REQUIREMENTS:
Be at least 18 years old and satisfy education and examination requirements. Contact license authority for additional requirements for endorsements.

EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
Completion of teacher preparation program at an approved educator preparation provider. Contact the licensing authority for additional requirements for endorsements and for updated requirements for the practitioner occupational teacher's license.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
Praxis Exams (Core Academic Skills & Specialty Area Tests) administered by the Educational Testing Services

RECIPROCITY WITH OTHER STATES:
Yes

47-3100000002.title: DENTAL ASSISTANTS
47-3100000002.description:
DENTAL ASSISTANTS

A dental assistant assists in the care of dental patients under the direct supervision of the dentist. A dental assistant may not remove hard or soft deposits by scaling or curettage from surfaces of teeth, and may not perform any dental function that requires professional judgment or skill. A dental assistant can perform coronal polishing, monitoring nitrous oxide sedation, expose radiographs, placing sealants, restorative or prosthetic function only if certified to do so by the Board.

REQUIREMENTS:
Be eighteen (18) years of age. Be of good moral character and reputation. Be a U.S. or Canadian citizen or entitled to live in the United States. Must have graduated high school or have gotten a GED.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
Successful completion of examinations administered by the course providers approved by the Board is required for each certification.

CONTINUING EDUCATION:
Must maintain current training in C.P.R.

RENEWAL REQUIREMENTS:
Every two years. License expires in birth month according to even or odd birth year.
47-3100000002.agency: Department of Health · Division of Health Related Boards · Division of Health Related Boards

47-2900000010.title: DENTAL HYGIENISTS
47-2900000010.description:
DENTAL HYGIENISTS
A person who engages in clinical procedures primarily concerned with the performance of preventive dental service not constituting the practice of dentistry, including removing of all hard and soft deposits and stains, polishing surfaces of teeth, performing clinical examinations of teeth and tissue for diagnosis by the dentist, and other procedures as delegated by the dentist under his direct supervision. May not perform dental functions requiring professional judgment or skill.

REQUIREMENTS:
Be at least 18 years of age, of good moral character and reputation, be a U.S. Citizen or have authority to work in the United States, satisfy education and examination requirements. (Limited licenses available for teaching do not require the examinations.)

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Graduation from a school of dental hygiene approved by the Board and accredited by the American Dental Association Commission on Dental Accreditation.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
The ADEX or Western Regional Examining Board examination is required for any applicant who has recently graduated or who does nothave a license in another state under which he/she had practice for three of the preceding five years. Any applicant who has failed any board approved exam must pass that exam in any case. The National Board examination is required for applicants who h…

47-2900000011.title: DENTIST
47-2900000011.description:
DENTIST

A dentist diagnoses, prescribes for or treats disease, pain, deformity, deficiency, injury, or physical condition of the human teeth or jaws or associated structures; extracts teeth, repairs or fills cavities, corrects malformations of teeth or jaws, performs oral surgery, takes impressions for replacement of teeth; furnishes or maintains dentures, bridges, crowns or other tooth substitutes; adjusts artificial replacement structures, gives interpretations of dental radiographs, or administers anesthetic other than topical for dental operations. A special permit is required to utilize general anesthesia on an outpatient basis or parenteral drugs for intravenous sedation. Certification specialities: Endodontics, Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, Oral Pathology, Pedodontics, Periodontics, Dedntal Publis Health, and Prosthodontics.

REQUIREMENTS:
Be at least 18 years of age, a citizen of the United States or Canada, of good moral character and reputation, and satisfy educational and examination requirements.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Pre-dental college program, graduation from a dental school approved by the American Dental Association. Specialty certifications require additional graduate study.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
The ADEX exam or Western Regional Examining Board (WREB) is required for any applicant who has recently graduated…

47-2900000012.title: DIETITIAN/NUTRITIONIST
47-2900000012.description:
DIETITIAN/NUTRITIONISTS

Dietitians and nutritionists provide medical nutrition therapy and nutritional education; set up and supervise food service systems for institutions such as hospitals, prisons and schools; do research; and develop and administer nutrition care standards and systems.

REQUIREMENTS:
Be at least 18 years of age, of good moral character and satisfy education, experience, and examination requirements.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Minimum of a baccalaureate degree in a program approved by the Board of Dietitian/Nutritionist Examiners.

EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENT:
As required by the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics (Formerly the American Dietetic Association). Must be completed prior to taking the examination.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
National examination administered by the Commission on Dietetic Registration of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics.

RENEWAL REQUIREMENTS:
Every two (2) years.

47-4300000002.title: EMERGENCY MEDICAL DISPATCHER
47-4300000002.description:
EMERGENCY MEDICAL DISPATCHER (EMD)

Receives calls for emergency medical services and dispatches aid following a Department of Health approved protocol system used by the employing dispatch agency, including systematized caller interrogation questions, systematized pre-arrival instructions, and protocols matching the dispatcher's evaluation of injury or illness severity with vehicle response mode and configuration.

PROSPECTIVE:
Any dispatching entity receiving and dispatching calls for emergency medical services which provides pre-arrival medical care instructions may require persons assigned to handle such calls to be certified.

REQUIREMENTS:
Completion of a Department approved EMD course, maintenance of proficiency in cardiopulmonary resuscitation for basic life support procedures, and either provide proof of having successfully certified as an EMD through an approved medical dispatch organization that has pre-qualified for certification reciprocity or satisfy the examination requirement; obtain a criminal background check conducted by the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation (TBI) and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI).

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENT:
Successful completion of an approved medical dispatch organization examination.

RENEWAL:
Recertification is required every two (2) years contingent on maintaining proficiency…

47-4700000005.title: LIMITED LICENSED ELECTRICIANS
47-4700000005.description:
LIMITED LICENSED ELECTRICIANS

The Limited Licensed Electrician (LLE) state license is only required by electricians performing work in a municipality utilizing the Division of Fire Prevention for permits, inspections and covers work less than $25,000 per project. Always first check with local government to see if they accept the LLE or if they have a local licensing requirement for permits and inspections. The LLE license is issued to individuals passing the LLE trade exam. The LLE license requirements is defined in T.C.A.  62-6-102(d) and  68-102-150.

REQUIREMENTS:
Photo-ID and Social Security Number. Exam (PSI is the exam vendor). Completed Application. Fee of $50.00 for two (2) year license.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
The Tennessee Limited License Electrician exam has 40 questions and a time limit of 2 hours. A score of 72.5% is required (29 correct). Topics covered on the exam are general knowledge, electrical installation requirements, services, feeders, branch circuits, over-current protection, grounding and bonding, conductors and cables, raceways and boxes, hazardous locations, special occupancies, special equipment, low voltage, alarms, signaling systems, communications, lighting, signs, and general use equipment.

As of this time Tennessee does not require continuing education for the Limite…

47-4700000001.title: ELEVATOR INSPECTOR
47-4700000001.description:
ELEVATOR INSPECTOR

An elevator inspector is an employee of Tennessee who is authorized to inspect elevators, escalators and new or altered dumbwaiters for compliance with state requirements. Inspectors must make or be present at all required inspections.

REQUIREMENTS:
Elevator inspectors are Qualified Elevator Inspector (QEI) certified. Present evidence satisfactory to the Board of experience in inspecting elevators and satisfy the examination requirement.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENT:
Satisfactory performance on an examination administered by the Qualified Elevator Inspector Training Fund (QEITF).

RENEWAL:
Annual training and renewal are required.
47-4700000001.agency: Department of Labor and Workforce Development · WRC Division

47-3900000006.title: EMBALMER
47-3900000006.description:
EMBALMER

Embalming is the art and science of preserving human remains by treating them (in its modern form with chemicals) to forestall decomposition. The intention is to keep the deceased suitable for public visitation at a funeral, for religious reasons or for medical and scientific purposes such as their use as anatomical specimens.

REQUIREMENTS:
1. Application
2. Application Fee
3. A copy of an official photo identification issued by a governmental agency, such as a valid (permanent, current, unexpired, legible) driver's license, U.S. passport or federal, state, county or city employee I.D. card showing the individuals date of birth and address
4. Two (2) letters of recommendation by a licensed funeral director and/or embalmer which attest to the good moral character and competence of the applicant. Such letters shall be signed and dated on printed stationery.
5. An official transcript evidencing an Associate of Arts degree by successful completion of a mortuary science program consisting of not less than sixty (60) semester hours, ninety (90) quarter hours or the equivalent, with a program accredited by the American Board of Funeral Service Education
6. National Board Exam (Science) passing score of 75
7. Tennessee Laws, Rules & Regulations Exam passing score of 75
8. Certification of Completion of Apprenticeship Form

47-3900000013.title: EMBALMER APPRENTICE
47-3900000013.description:
EMBALMER APPRENTICE

Apprentice" means a person registered as an apprentice pursuant to T.C.A. 62-5-312.

An apprentice funeral director is a registered individual who specializes in assisting the funeral director or embalmer in all aspects associated with funeral services. An apprentice may assist a funeral director with:
Support to the bereaved during initial stages of their grief
Arrangements and direction of funeral services
Removal of the deceased from the place of death
Filing death certificates

An apprentice embalmer may assist with the art and science of preserving human remains by treating them (in its modern form with chemicals) to forestall decomposition. The intention is to keep the deceased suitable for public visitation at a funeral for religious reasons or for medical and scientific purposes such as their use as anatomical specimens.

REQUIREMENTS:
1) An official transcript from an educational institution showing the applicant has graduated from a High School or has earned a GED recognized by a State Department of Education must be received by the Board office prior to approval of the Apprentice / Student application.
2) If you answered YES to the felony / misdemeanor question involving moral turpitude you must attach a written statement explaining the circumstances of each incident. A copy of the official document…

47-2900000015.title: EMERGENCY MEDICAL RESPONDER
47-2900000015.description:
EMERGENCY MEDICAL RESPONDER (EMR)

An emergency medical responder participates in an organized program of mobile pre-hospital emergency medical care to the sick and injured individuals before a licensed Basic or Advance Life Support unit arrives. Professional may provide additional procedures with devices and supplies consigned under medical direction if trained in an appropriate program authorized by the Office of Emergency Medical Services.

REQUIREMENTS:
Certification by a certified instructor of an approved course of instruction for emergency providers that applicant is 18 years of age; is able to read, write and speak the English language; is currently certified in Basic Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation; and has attended all classes in training with one allowable absence, has completed practical skills evaluation, and has performed satisfactorily on all in-class examinations. In addition the applicant must satisfy the examination requirement.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENT:
A score of 70% on a written examination through the National Registry of Emergency Medical Technicians (NREMT).

RENEWAL REQUIREMENTS:
Successful completion of a refresher training course of at least 16 hours meeting the refresher course curriculum approved by the EMS Board OR Satisfactory completion (70% score) of the written examination for EMR's through NREMT.

47-2900000016.title: EMERGENCY MEDICAL TECHNICIAN - ADVANCED (EMT-A)
47-2900000016.description:
EMERGENCY MEDICAL TECHNICIAN - ADVANCED (EMT-A)

(formerly EMT-IV) An advanced emergency medical technician begins IVs and administers fluids for shock treatment and other medical purposes. Performs functions as any licensed EMT, i.e. performs an initial patient survey, provides emergency care and recognizes injuries and illness; gains knowledge of pre-existing medical conditions, previously prescribed medications, medical preference, and ID of the patient; performs, under authorized medical control, skills or procedures for which he has qualified by training and examination.

At least 18 years old; high school graduate or GED, ability to read, write and speak the English language; two (2) recent (within the preceding 12 months) original letters from medical professionals attesting to applicant's personal character; have no history within 3 years of habitual intoxication, personal misuse of drugs or intoxicating liquors, narcotics, controlled substances or other drugs or stimulants so as to adversely affect ability to perform as an AEMT; physical health adequate to provide patient care, absence of communicable diseases, and suitable emotional fitness to provide for the care and lifting of the ill or injured; obtain a criminal background check conducted by the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation (TBI) and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI); m…

47-2900000018.description:
EMERGENCY MEDICAL TECHNICIAN - PARAMEDIC (EMT-P)

An EMT-Paramedic performs an initial patient survey, provides emergency care through assessment of patient, recognizes injuries and illness, gains knowledge of pre-existing medical conditions, previously prescribed medications, medical preference, and ID of patient. An EMT-P performs specified procedures under authorized medical control.

REQUIREMENTS:
At least 18 years of age; high school graduate or have GED, and be able to read, write and speak the English language; two (2) recent (within the preceding 12 months) original letters from medical professionals attesting to applicant's personal character; have no history within 3 years of habitual intoxication or personal misuse of any drugs or use of intoxicating liquors, narcotics, controlled substances or other drugs or stimulants in such manner as to adversely affect ability to practice as a EMT-P; be of physical health adequate to conduct activities associated with patient care, including visual acuity, speech and hearing, use of all extremities, absence of musculoskeletal deformities, absence of communicable diseases, and suitable emotional fitness to provide for the care and lifting of the ill or injured; obtain a criminal background check conducted by the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation (TBI) and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI); meet certifica…

47-2900000017.title: EMERGENCY MEDICAL TECHNICIAN (EMT)
47-2900000017.description:
EMERGENCY MEDICAL TECHNICIAN (EMT)

An EMT performs an initial patient survey, provides emergency care and recognizes injuries and illness. The EMT gains knowledge of pre-existing medical conditions, previously prescribed medications, medical preference, and ID of the patient. An EMT performs, under authorized medical control, skills or procedures for which he has qualified by training and examination.

REQUIREMENTS:
At least 18 years of age; high school graduate or have a general equivalency diploma (GED), and be able to read, write and speak the English language; have no history within 3 years of habitual intoxication or personal misuse of any drugs or use of intoxicating liquors, narcotics, controlled substances or other drugs or stimulants so as to adversely affect ability to perform as an EMT; be of physical health adequate to provide patient care, absence of communicable diseases, and suitable emotional fitness to provide for the care and lifting of the ill or injured; obtain a criminal background check conducted by the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation (TBI) and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI); and satisfy training and examination requirements.

TRAINING REQUIREMENTS:
Must successfully complete an approved basic Emergency Medical Technician course including all required examinations within two (2) year of completion of training.

47-2900000052.description:
EMERGENCY MEDICAL TECHNICIAN PARAMEDIC - CRITICAL CARE (EMTP-CC)

An EMTP-CC performs an initial patient survey, provides emergency care through assessment of patient, recognizes injuries and illness, gains knowledge of pre-existing medical conditions, previously prescribed medications, medical preference, and ID of patient and provides on-going care of critically injured or ill patients. An EMTP-CC performs specified procedures under authorized medical control.

REQUIREMENTS:
At least 18 years of age; high school graduate or have GED, and be able to read, write and speak the English language; two (2) recent (within the preceding 12 months) original letters from medical professionals attesting to applicant's personal character; have no history within 3 years of habitual intoxication or personal misuse of any drugs or use of intoxicating liquors, narcotics, controlled substances or other drugs or stimulants in such manner as to adversely affect ability to practice as a EMTP-CC; be of physical health adequate to conduct activities associated with patient care, including visual acuity, speech and hearing, use of all extremities, absence of musculoskeletal deformities, absence of communicable diseases, and suitable emotional fitness to provide for the care and lifting of the ill or injured; obtain a criminal background check conducted by the Tennessee Bureau of In…

47-3100000001.title: AESTHETICIAN
47-3100000001.description:
AESTHETICIAN

An aesthetician does one or more of the following: massages, cleans, stimulates, manipulates, exercises, beautifies or performs similar work with hands or mechanical or electrical apparatus or by use of cosmetic preparations, tonics, lotions or creams; places or applies artificial eyelashes, gives facials, applies makeup, gives skin care or removes superfluous hair by tweezing, depilatories or waxing.

REQUIREMENTS:
Be at least sixteen years of age having completed and passed a course of instruction of not less than 750 hours in the practice and theory of aesthetics at a school of cosmetology.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
A written and practical examination is required Total included with Cosemetologists.
47-3100000001.agency: Department of Commerce and Insurance · Division of Regulatory Boards · Division of Regulatory Boards

47-3900000015.title: EYELASH SPECIALIST
47-3900000015.description:
EYELASH SPECIALIST

A nonrefundable, nontransferable application/examination fee as set by the board. Satisfactory proof that the applicant is at least sixteen (16) years of age and has completed and passed a course of instruction of no less than three hundred (300) hours in classroom instruction and practical experience, including at least eight (8) hours of theoretical instruction, and that includes instruction in the following areas: Recognizing infectious or contagious diseases of the eye and allergic reactions to materials, Proper sanitation practices, Occupational health and safety practices, Eyelash extension application procedures; and, Eyelash extension isolation and separation procedures; and Satisfactory proof that the applicant successfully completed, as part of the hours of instruction described in subdivision (f)(2), up to one (1) hour of online or in-person training, at no cost to the applicant, by a nonprofit anti-domestic violence organization recognized by the Tennessee Coalition to End Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault on domestic violence that focuses on how to recognize the signs of domestic violence, how to respond to these signs, and how to refer a client to resources for victims of domestic violence

47-1300000008.title: INVESTMENT ADVISOR REPRESENTATIVE
47-1300000008.description:
INVESTMENT ADVISER REPRESENTATIVE

Any partner, officer, or director of (or person occupying a similar status or performing similar functions) an investment adviser, or other individual, except clerical or ministerial personnel, who is employed by or associated with an investment adviser.

REQUIREMENTS:
1. A Form U4 and all information and exhibits required by such form;
2. The appropriate application fee as set forth by the Act;
3. Satisfactory evidence of a passing score by the applicant on the appropriate examinations; and
4. Such other information as the Division may request of a particular applicant to determine eligibility for registration.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
(a) Each applicant for initial registration as an investment adviser representative:

Nothing in this section shall be construed to permit the treatment of any mental, emotional or adjustment disorder other than marital problems, parent-child problems, child, and adolescent antisocial behavior, adult antisocial behavior, other specified family circumstances, other interpersonal problems, phase of life problems, other life circumstance problems, occupational problems, and uncomplicated bereavement. 47-3100000003.title: MASSAGE THERAPIST
47-3100000003.description:
MASSAGE THERAPIST

A massage therapist is a person who is licensed by the board and who practices massage for compensation. Massage means the manipulation of the soft tissues of the body with the intention of positivelyt affecting the health and well being of the client.

REQUIREMENTS:
Be at least 18 years of age; of good moral character, free of conviction of the offense of prostitution or sexual misconduct; satisfy education or experience requirements.

EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
Successfully complete the curriculum of one or more postsecondary academic institutions for massage, bodywork, and/or somatic therapy totaling 500 hours or more, where the institution is approved by the Tennessee Higher Education Commission or its equivalent in another state.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
Massage and Bodyworks Licensing Examination (MBLEx). A temporary license may be issued if a person works at all times under the supervision of a licensed person and successfully completes an exam.

RENEWAL:
Renewal is required every two years and is contingent on satisfying continuing education requirements.

CONTINUING EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
All licensees must complete twenty-five (25) hours of continuing education every two (2) calendar years.

00-52.title: Assistant Engineer (Limited - Oceans)
00-52.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as an Assistant Engineer (Limited - Oceans) include 1,080 days at sea, with 540 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. 00-47.title: First Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-47.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a First Assistant Engineer - Upper Level, the applicant must complete 360 days of service as a Second or Third Assistant Engineer; while holding a Second Assistant Engineer license. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. 00-49.title: Third Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-49.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Third Assistant Engineer (upper Level, the applicant must complete one of the following: 1080 days of service in the engine room with 720 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED); or 1080 days as a machinist apprentice engaged in construction or repair of marine, locomotive, or stationary engines plus 360 days of sea service in an engine room as oiler, watertender, or jr. engineer; or graduate from an approved course of studies. 47-3100000008.description:

A chiropractic assistant may offer physical agent modalities and rehabilitation advice and services to the public, specifically and only on orders from a duly licensed physician.

Be at least 18 years of age, of good moral character, and satisfy the education and examination requirements.

Must have 50 hours of instruction approved by the Board.

Completion of 1200 hours of clinical internship under direct supervision of a chiropractic physician.

Applicants for certification will be required to successfully complete a board-approved examination with a minimum score of seventy-five (75).RENEWAL:

47-3100000011.description:
MEDICATION AIDE

Certified medication aides, also known as CMAs, administer medications of all kinds to patients. Hospitals, nursing homes, and medical facilities hire certified medication aides to work full-time flexible shifts including nights and weekends. Certified medication aides work in clinical settings within a collaborative team environment where they interact with other medical staff members. They do not travel outside of the facility to perform their regular tasks. Certified medication aides usually report to the nursing supervisor on duty.

REQUIREMENTS:
Is at least eighteen (18) years of age. Has completed the twelfth (12th) grade or its equivalent or has successfully passed the test for and has received a general equivalency diploma. Is a certified nurse aide or licensed occupational therapy assistant. Has practiced continuously as a certified nurse aide or a licensed occupational therapy assistant in a nursing home, PACE, or assisted care living facility for at one year Have a recommendation from a facility where the individual is employed or contracted . Has successfully completed a course of instruction of a training program approved by the Board of at least 60 hours of instruction, consisting of 40 classroom hours and twenty clinical hours (i). Has passed a standardized examination.

47-2900000053.description:
PODIATRIC X-RAY OPERATORS

Means one who applies x-rays to human beings for diagnostic purposes in a podiatrist's office in Tennessee must be certified by the Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners.

REQUIREMENTS:
Be at least 18 years of age, possess a high school diploma or its equivalent, and satisfy the educational, training and examination requirements.

EDUCATIONAL , TRAINING, AND EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
Successful completion of six (6) contact hours of didactic instructions in the field of x-ray operation, successful completion of at least sixty (60) hours of supervised clinical experience.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
The applicant must successfully complete an examination approved by the Board.

Must biennially complete four (4) hours of radiological related continuing education in courses provided or sponsored by the APMA.

47-1900000001.title: PSYCHOLOGICAL ASSISTANT
47-1900000001.description:
PSYCHOLOGICAL ASSISTANT

A Psychological Assistant is a person who holds himself out to be a Psychological Assistant and/or renders to individuals or to the public for remuneration any service involving the application of recognized principles, methods, and procedures of the science and profession of psychology and only under the direct employment and supervision of either the Psychologist employing the Psychological Assistant or the employing community mental health center or state governmental agency.

EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
A minimum of one (1) academic year of graduate training in psychology, including a master's degree from an accredited institution of high education is required. In lieu of a master's degree, an applicant who has successfully completed a minimum of thirty-three (33) graduate semester hours in residence as a matriculated student in a doctoral program in psychology may be considered for certification.

RENEWAL REQUIREMENTS:
Renewal required by expiration date.
