47-2900000044.description:
LICENSED CERTIFIED RESPIRATORY THERAPIST

Under the supervision of a physician, a certified respiratory therapist may assume clinical responsibility for specified respiratory care modalities involving the application of well-defined therapeutic techniques. The technician shall not be required to exercise independent clinical judgment; however a technician may be expected to adjust or modify therapeutic techniques within well-defined procedures based on a limited range of patient responses. The technician may accept telephone or verbal orders and responsibilities involving the supervision of respiratory care therapists and respiratory care assistants.

REQUIREMENTS:
Certification as an entry level respiratory therapy practitioner (CRTT) by the National Board for Respiratory Care.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
Passing he entry level examination provided by the National Board of Respiratory Care (NBRC) obtaining the registry credential of CRT.

A respiratory therapist may, under the supervision of a physician, exercise considerable independent clinical judgement in the respiratory care of patients. The therapist is capable of serving as a technical resource person to the physician regarding current practices in respiratory care and to the hospital staff regarding effective and safe methods for administering respiratory care.

REQUIREMENTS
Satisfy education and examination requirements.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Successful completion of a respiratory care therapist or technician academic and clinical preparation program approved by the American Medical Association.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
Successful completion of the advanced practice examination system provided by the National Board for Respiratory Care (NBRC) obtaining the registry credential or RRT.

The assistant may be expected to adjust or modify therapeutic techniques within well-defined procedures based on a limited range of patient responses under the supervision of a respiratory care therapist, respiratory care technician, or physician experienced in respiratory care. An assistant must have passed the critical care section of the council approved examination for respiratory care assistants to perform functions on a critical care patient being maintained on mechanical ventilation.

Satisfy training and examination requirements.

On-the-job training equivalent to at least 1,000 hours of clinical training in respiratory care during a period of 18 consecutive months under the supervision of a respiratory care therapist, a respiratory care technician, or a licensed physician experienced in respiratory care.

A passing score on the National Board for Respiratory Care (NBRC) entry level examination.

47-2900000064.title: Medical Surgical Assistant Registry
47-2900000064.description:
MEDICAL SURGICAL ASSISTANT REGISTRY

Medical Surgical assistants work in operating rooms assisting surgeons by preparing the necessary equipment, helping position and draping patients, providing needed instruments during the operation and keeping the area sterile. Surgical assistants usually have prior medical training, along with formal training in the surgical assisting discipline.

Candidates for a surgical assisting certificate may enroll in an undergraduate or graduate level program depending on prior education completed. Common courses include anesthetics and anesthesia methods, surgical complications, clinical computer applications, medical ethics and operating room procedures. Most programs require students to complete a minimum number of hours in a clinical setting.

Performs tests in a limited range in a new emerging technology in the clinical laboratory in a subspecialty not otherwise regulated. Procedures must not be components of the traditional clinical laboratory science body of knowledge contained in chemistry, hematology, microbiology or immunhematology. A cytology general supervisor is a qualified cytotechnologist responsible for day-to-day supervision or oversight of the laboratory operation and personnel performing testing and reporting test results in cytology. (For the subspecialty of cytology a lab must have a general supervisor.)

00-10.description: Nuclear Facility Operators are required to have either training or experience to become licensed. They must pass a medical exam, a written test, and an operating test. Nuclear Facility Senior Operators have additional experience and pass another exam to be promoted from Nuclear Facility Operators. 47-2900000003.description:
ADVANCED PRACTICE REGISTERED NURSE

An Advanced Practice Nurse (APN) is a Tennessee licensed registered nurse who has a master's degree or higher in a nursing specialty and has national specialty certification as a nurse practitioner, nurse anesthetist, nurse midwife, or clinical nurse specialist.

EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
Master's Degree or higher in one of the four advanced practice nursing roles/categories: Clinical Nurse Specialist, Nurse Anesthetist, Nurse Midwife, and Nurse Practitioner.

00-63.description: A Hospital Corpsman is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A hospital corpsman must have U.S. military experience as and a rating of hospital corpsman or Health Services Technician or equivalent. 47-3100000010.description:
CERTIFIED MEDICAL ASSISTANT

A certified medical assistant has training to function in an assistive role to a licensed physician or licensed nurse in the provision of patient care activities in a facility used as an ambulatory outpatient hospital clinic as delegated by the physician or licensed nurse. They shall not administer medications to hospital inpatients or patients in an emergency department.

Certification by the American Board of Industrial Hygiene as a Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH) or Industrial Hygienist in Training (IHIT) OR Satisfaction of education and experience requirements below.

Degree from an accredited college/university in industrial hygiene, engineering, chemistry, physics, biology, medicine, or related physical or biological science and acquisition, through special studies and training, of competence in recognizing environmental stresses in the workplace, understanding their effects, evaluating on the basis of experience and with the aid of quantitative measures and techniques the magnitude of such stresses in terms of ability to impair health and well-being, and prescribing methods to eliminate, control or reduce such stress when necessary to alleviate their effects.

OCCUPATIONAL THERAPIST

An occupational therapist is engaged in evaluation, treatment or consultation regarding specific occupational therapy services. The occupational therapist may teach daily living skills, develop perceptual and motor skills, and develop prevocational and avocational abilities.

REQUIREMENTS:
Be at least 18 years of age and satisfy experience, education, and examination requirements. Successful completion of at least six (6) months of supervised field work.

47-2900000013.description:
DISPENSING OPTICIANS

Opticians make and dispense eyeglasses/contact lenses from a doctor's prescription. They can also fit eye glasses to the face. They do not write prescriptions or fit contacts to the eyes.

Be 18 years of age and satisfy education and experience and examination requirements.

OPTOMETRIST

47-2900000030.description:
ORTHOTIST

An orthotist is an allied health professional who is specifically trained and educated to provide or manage the provision of a custom-designed, fabricated, modified and fitted external orthosis to an orthotics patient, based on a clinical assessment and a prescription from a health care practitioner authorized by law to write such prescriptions, to restore physiological function or cosmesis.

EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
Baccalaureate degree and completion of an othotics education program which is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Allied Health Education Programs or its successor organization. Successful completion of a clinical residency in orthotics and all examinations required by Rule 1155-4-.08.

RENEWAL REQUIREMENTS:
Renewal required by expiration date.

47-2900000032.description:
PEDORTHIST

47-2900000040.description:
PROSTHETIST

A prosthetist is an allied health professional who is specifically trained and educated to provide or manage the provision of a custom designed, fabricated, modified, and fitted external limb prosthesis to a prosthetic patient, based on a clinical assessment and a prescription from a health care practitioner authorized to write such prescriptions, to restore physiological function or cosmesis.

EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
Baccalaureate degree and completion of a prosthetic education program which is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Allied Health Education Programs or its successor organization. Successful completion of a clinical residency in prosthetics and all examinations required by Rule 1155-4-.08.

47-3100000006.title: OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY ASSISTANT
47-3100000006.description:
OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY ASSISTANT

An occupational therapy assistant assists in the practice of occupational therapy, which may include assisting in the evaluation, treatment and consultation regarding specific occupational therapy services; may teach daily living skills and developing perceptual motor skills, and pre-vocational and vocational abilities, under the supervision of an Occupational Therapist licensed in Tennessee.

REQUIREMENTS:
Be at least 18 years of age, of good moral character, and satisfy the education and examination requirements.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Successfully complete the academic requirements of an educational program in occupational therapy or occupational therapy assistant approved by the Board of Occupational Therapy and accredited by the Commission on Allied Health Education and Accreditation of the American Medical Association in collaboration with the American Occupational Therapy Association.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
The Occupational Therapy Registration examination administered by The National Board of Occupational Therapy (NBCOT). A letter of moral character is required for examination applicants.

Every two years.

47-1900000006.description:
PEST CONTROL CONSULTANT

A pest control consultant offers consultation to operators and aerial applicators in a field of pest control. A consultant is not authorized to apply pesticides for a fee.

REQUIREMENTS:
Must be commercially certified and prove to the satisfaction of the Pest Control Board that he/she possesses sufficient education to perform as a licensed consultant. This most frequently is proof of a four-year degree in the field of pest control in which consultation is offered, such as entomology.

47-3700000002.title: PEST CONTROL OPERATOR
47-3700000002.description:
PEST CONTROL OPERATOR

A Pest Control Operator applies, for a fee for any substance or mixture of substances or chemicals intended for defoliating or desiccating plants, or for preventing, destroying, repelling, or mitigating any insects, rodents, fungi, bacteria, weeds or other forms of plant or animal life declared a pest by the Commissioner of Agriculture. Licensing is for one or more categories specified. Must be 18 years of age prior to becoming licensed to apply general or restricted use pesticides. Supervises technicians.

REQUIREMENTS:
Satisfy education and experience and examination requirements.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:
A degree or its equivalent with a major or minor in a discipline reasonably related to the category of pest OR at least two years of full time verifiable work experience under a licensee in the category of license applying for in compliance with the rule except the categories of Agricultural-- Ground Equipment and Horticulture-- Lawn and Turf OR a combination of experience, education or 24 continuing education units.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:

47-3700000003.title: PEST CONTROL SOLICITOR/TECHNICIAN
47-3700000003.description:
PEST CONTROL SOLICITOR/TECHNICIAN

A pest control solicitor/technician performs duties of a pest control solicitor, pest control technician, or both. A solicitor is a salesperson or agent employed by a chartered pest control business who is authorized to solicit business or any employee authorized to enter into a pest control contract on behalf of a chartered pest control business.

REQUIREMENTS:
A solicitor must possess commercial certification in each category of service offered for sale or provided and be registered by the holder of the charter. Certification, required of a technician, is attained by completing the examination requirements and must be 16 years of age.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
Pass the CORE and category applicable to work. The CORE part covers general knowledge of pest control materials, safety methods and label interpretation and the category part tests knowledge relating to the specific category or categories in which the applicant is seeking a certification. An applicant may be tested in as many categories as desired within the time allowed. The examination must be taken every three years if the required number of continuing education units are not accrued to maintain certification.

RENEWAL REQUIREMENTS:
The renewal fees are staggered. Contact the registration authority for additional information.

47-2900000034.title: PHARMACIST
47-2900000034.description:
PHARMACIST

A pharmacist prepares, compounds, and dispenses drugs and devices, whether dispensed on the prescription of a medical practitioner or legally dispensed or sold directly to the ultimate consumer; insures the proper and safe storage and distribution of drugs; maintains proper records and relates information as required concerning such drugs and medicines and their therapeutic values and uses in the treatment and prevention of disease.

REQUIREMENTS:
Be at least 21 years of age and satisfy the experience, education and examination requirements.

EXPERIENCE:
Fifteen hundred (1,500) hours internship.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Graduate of an accredited College of Pharmacy (BS or Pharm. D degree)

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
National licensing examination (NAPLEX) administered several times each year.

CONTINUING EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
Thirty (30) contact hours each two (2) years of which fifteen (15) shall be in line contact programs as determined by the ACPE designation. A maximum of six (6) contact hours may be approved for programs approved by the board.

RECIPROCITY WITH OTHER STATES:
All states except California and Florida.

47-2900000063.title: Pharmacy Technician
47-2900000063.description:
PHARMACY TECHNICAN

A pharmacy technician assists a pharmacist with the preparation of prescription medications for customers. He or she may receive written prescription requests from or may process requests doctors' offices that have been sent electronically or phoned in. A pharmacy technician generally performs the following duties. Pharmacy technicians may: Fill bottles with doctor-prescribed medications, type and apply labels with directions and other information for patients, and pre-pack bulk medications. Handle any required cash register operations. Resolve issues, concerns or complaints made by customers .Call doctors for prescription refill authorizations. Type up prescription information details to produce labels for packages. Keep detailed records of on-hand medications and other stock. Resolve any issues with patients' insurance coverage.

REQUIREMENTS
Initial application must be submitted online: declaration of citizenship form signed and notarized, a copy of their valid government issued identification, criminal background and license fee.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Pharmacy technicians typically need a high school diploma or equivalent. Many pharmacy technicians receive only on-the-job training, although many employers prefer to hire applicants who have attended a formal training program.

00-80.description: A Marine Physician Assistant is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). 47-2900000037.description:
PHYSICIAN ASSISTANTS

Physician Assistants provide patient services under the written protocol and responsibility of a doctor of medicine or osteopathy; can elicit detailed patient histories and do complete physical examinations; can reach tentative diagnoses and order appropriate laboratory tests; and initiate appropriate treatment using protocol. A physician's assistant may qualify for limited authority to write prescriptions. A license is required for performance of duties under the provision of the applicable law. Can use designation PA or Physician Assistant.

REQUIREMENTS:
The applicant must submit evidence of good moral character, and that he or she has met the educational and examination requirements. In addition, the applicant must designate a primary supervising physician. Temporary licenses are issued to applicants who have completed the educational requirement or are licensed in another state under certain restrictions.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

For new licenses, graduation from an accredited physician assistant training program is required.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
Examination of the National Commission on the Certification of Physician Assistant (NCCPA).

00-31.title: Tankerman
00-31.description: Tankerman refers to several endorsements or qualified ratings to Merchant Marine Documents (MMD). All Tankerman endorsements require qualifying experience, training in firefighting and cargo (dangerous liquids or liquefied gasses), and passing an exam. Endorsements include Tankerman - Person-In-Charge (Tankerman PIC), Tankerman-Engineer, Tankerman Assistant, and Tankerman - PIC (Barge). Tankerman endorsements are valid for the duration of the MMD, which is issued for 5 years. Renewal of certification requires meeting all the requirements to renew the MMD and either have recent qualifying experience or training. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR13.109) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr13_02.html.

47-4700000007.description:
LIMITED LICENSED PLUMBERS

The Limited Licensed Plumber (LLP) state license is only required by plumbers performing work in a municipality utilizing the Division of Fire Prevention for permits, inspections and covers work less than $25,000 per project; general maintenance work, less than $500 is exempt from the LLP license.
Always check with local government to see if they accept the LLP or if they have local licensing requirements for permits and inspections. The LLP license is issued to individuals passing the LLP trade exam. More information can be found in T.C.A.  62-6-403.

Photo-ID and Social Security Number. Exam (PSI is the exam vendor). Completed Application. Fee of $75.00 for two (2) year license. A Business" tax license may also be required by local government.

PODIATRIST

Means one who examines, diagnoses, or treats medically, mechanically, or surgically, the ailments of the human foot, ankle and soft tissue structures extending no higher than the distal tibial metaphyseal flair, including the use and prescribing of drugs and medications, but excluding the direct applications of general anesthesia by a podiatrist and the amputation of the foot. Be at least 18 years of age, have completed at least a one year of residency, and satisfy education and examination requirements.

Graduate from a podiatric medical college accredited by the Council on Podiatric Medical Education and American Podiatric Medical Association. The educational requirements must be completed prior to the date of application.

Engages in the business or accepts employment to obtain or furnish information on any of: Crime or wrongs done or threatened against the United States or any state or territory of the United states; The identity, habits, conduct, business, occupation, honesty, integrity, credibility, knowledge, trustworthiness, efficiency, loyalty, activity, movement, whereabouts, affiliations, associations, transactions, acts, reputations or character of any person; The location, disposition or recovery of lost or stolen property; The cause or responsibility for fires, libels, losses, accidents, damages or injuries to persons or to property; or The securing of evidence to be used before any court, board, commission, officer or investigating committee. PRIVATE INVESTIGATOR CERTIFIED TRAINER

Any individua/company who offers private investigative training for a fee must be certified by the Commission as being qualified to administer and certify to successful completion of the training. A person who offers private investigators training for a fee and is not an employee of a private investigative, or proprietary, agency must be licensed as a training school This requirement does not include individuals who offer continuing professional education programs. Render general misdemeanor probation supervision, counseling and collection services to the courts.

An initial criminal record search and maintaining a criminal record free of any felony conviction. Complete forty hours of orientation by the private probation services company.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Each employee who is responsible for providing probation supervision shall have at least four (4) years of experience in a criminal justice or a social services agency providing counseling services or shall have a bachelor's and/or an associate's degree from an accredited college or university.

None.

Operates x-ray equipment for making images of the skeletal system for diagnostic purposes. May offer chiropractic x-ray technologist advice and services to the public, specifically and only on orders from a duly licensed chiropractic physician.

47-2900000041.description:

A radiologist assistant is an advanced-level radiologic technologist who enhances patient care by extending the capacity of the radiologist in the diagnostic imaging environment. The radiologist assistant is an A.R.R.T.-certified (American Registry of Radiologic Technologists) radiographer who has completed an advanced academic program encompassing a nationally recognized radiologist assistant curriculum and a radiologist-directed clinical preceptorship. With radiologist supervision, the radiologist assistant performs patient assessment, patient management, fluoroscopy and other radiology procedures. The radiologist assistant also makes initial observations of diagnostic images, but does not provide an official interpretation (final written report) as defined by the ACR Standard for Communication, Diagnostic Radiology.

Graduation from a radiologist assistant educational program and a radiologist directed clinical preceptorship leading to a baccalaureate degree or equivalent from an institution offering a program accredited by an entity recognized by the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists for certification purposes.

Any person who is not a licensed real estate broker or affiliate broker and who engages in or is employed in the business of locating, providing assistance in locating, or furnishing information concerning the location or availability of real property, including apartment housing, which may be leased or rented as a private dwelling, abode or place of residence and who receives or solicits a fee or other valuable consideration from a prospective tenant.

A Motor Vehicle Salesperson includes any person employed by a licensed motor vehicle dealer who is engaged in the business of effecting or attempting to effect the sale or purchase of motor vehicles or recreational vehicles owned by some other person to residents of the state, for which service some form of remuneration is expected, whether the remuneration be designated as a salary, fee, commission, rental or otherwise, and regardless of whether the remuneration is paid by the buyer, seller or a third party.

00-61.description: A ship's Professional Nurse is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A professional nurse must also hold a valid license as a registered nurse issued within the United States. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.

47-2900000043.title: REGISTERED NURSE
47-2900000043.description:
REGISTERED NURSE

A registered nurse diagnoses and treats human responses to actual or potential physical and emotional health problems; may administer drugs; may assist in convalescence and rehabilitation; may provide health teaching, counseling, and other services designed to improve a patient's well-being; and may work in hospitals, nursing homes, clinics, schools, retirement communities, health insurance organizations, or private residences.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
A nursing degree from an approved nursing school within a college or university.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
National Council Licensure Examination (NCLEX-RNr). A person who has been approved to take the registered nursing exam can practice as a "graduate nurse" without a license for 120 days if they graduated from a nursing program in the last 90 days.

CONTINUING EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
Must maintain competency requirements.

RENEWAL:
Renew every two years.

47-2900000055.description:

An RN first assistant, or RNFA, works alongside the surgeon in the operating room providing direct patient care. Nurses need extensive surgical experience and additional training to qualify as first assistants, and many nurses get certification in perioperative nursing or obtain credentials as advanced practice nurses.

If the candidate attends an out of state school, the candidate will use a paper form to verify that the candidate has met degree requirements. The candidate can request an application packet from the Board. Fingerprinting is a required part of the process. Tennessee's vendor for electronic fingerprinting is Identogo. Then the candidate will wait for an ATT which will allow them to schedule. The Tennessee Board will receive official examination results. Once the license has been issued, it can be verified online. 00-03.title: Able Seaman - AB
00-03.description: Requirements for an Able Seaman license include a medical certificate of excellent health, and a certificate attesting to vision, color perception, and general physical condition. While no experience or formal schooling is required, training at a union-operated school is the best source. With experience at sea, and perhaps union-sponsored training, an ordinary seaman with a Merchant Marine Document (MMD) can pass the Able Seaman exam and move up with 3 years of service. Please see the U.S. Coast Guard web site at: http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, the Veteran's Employment and Training Service (VETS) web site at http://umet-vets.dol.gov/ableseaman.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html

00-30.title: Lifeboatman - LBMAN
00-30.description: A person with a Merchant Marine Document (MMD) with one year of experience at sea in the deck department, two years experience in any other department on vessels greater than 100 gross tons, or who has completed a USCG approved course and 3 months of sea experience may take written and practical exams to be endorsed with the qualified rating of Lifeboatman (LB). An MMD with a qualified rating is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through documented recent experience, pass an exam, or complete a training course. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR12.10-7) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-30.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-33.title: Merchant Mariner's Document - MMD
00-33.description: The United States Coast Guard issues a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) to unlicensed personnel who support the operation of a vessel. Unqualified ratings are issued to entry level individuals who typically have little or no sea service for the following rating types: ordinary seaman (deck department), wiper (engineering department), or food handler (steward's department). Qualified ratings are issued based on previous sea service in a particular department or specialized training. Qualified ratings for members in the deck department are issued by rating type (e.g. Able Seaman) and vessel type restrictions (e.g. sail vessels or offshore supply vessels). Qualified ratings for members in the engineering department are issued by type (e.g. Qualified Member of the Engine Department) and specific rating (e.g. oiler, fireman/watertender, junior engineer, deck engine mechanic, or engineman). Other ratings are issued for specialized training or experience, such as Lifeboatman, Tankerman, or GMDSS At-Sea Maintainer. An MMD is valid for 5 years and may be renewed. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-33.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-04.title: Ordinary Seaman
00-04.description: An Ordinary Seaman is a person holding a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) issued by the United States Coast Guard without qualified ratings. This is an entry level MMD and does not require maritime experience or a physical examination, but will require proof that the applicant has passed a chemical test for dangerous drugs. While no training is required, a union-operated school can provide useful background knowledge. An MMD is valid for 5 years and may be renewed. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.

00-32.title: Qualified Member of the Engine Department - QMED
00-32.description: Qualified Member of the Engine Department - QMED A person with a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) having at least 6 months of underway service working as a wiper or coal passer in the engineering department may take a written exam and at least one rating exam (Fireman/Watertender, Oiler, Deck Engineer, Junior Engineer, Refrigeration Engineer, Electrician, Machinist, or Pumpman) to be endorsed as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Additional experience is required for some endorsements. Renewal of certification requires meeting all the requirements to renew the MMD and either have recent qualifying experience or training. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.15-11) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.

47-4100000030.description:
REGISTERED SCRAP METAL DEALER

A scrap metal dealer is any person, including any corporation, firm, company or association or an employee or agent who has the express or implied authority to buy, exchange or deal in scrap metal on behalf of the dealer. The business and any other person or entity acting as a scrap metal dealer or on behalf of the scrap metal business must register with the Department of Commerce and Insurance. They must understand how adults learn and how to create a professional learning environment where all adults are constantly improving their own knowledge and skills. He or she must put curriculum and instruction first. A learning-centered leader understands what students should be learning and how 21st century students learn best. Learning-centered instructional leaders require access to top notch professional development (PD) experiences.

An individual who represents a broker-dealer in effecting or attempting to effect purchases or sales of securities from, in, or into this state.

REQUIREMENTS:
Be at least 21 years of age, a U.S. citizen or resident alien, legally mentally competent, free of habitual drunkenness or narcotics addiction or dependence, of good moral character, meet statutory insurance requirements, and satisfy the experience or examination requirement. 00-29.description: Licensure as an Ocean Transportation Intermediary (OTI)- Non-Vessel-Operating Common Carrier (NVOCC) requires that the qualifying individual for the company have three years of qualifying experience, meet character requirements, and be bonded. The license is issued indefinitely or until revoked or suspended. Details can be found at the FMC web sites: http://www.fmc.gov/cfr/515.htm, http://www.fmc.gov/Help/OTI.htm, and the Code of Federal Regulations (46CFR515) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr515_02.html.
00-29.agency: Federal Maritime Commission · Bureau of Tariffs, Certification and Licensing

47-4100000002.title: AFFILIATE AUCTIONEER
47-4100000002.description:
AFFILIATE AUCTIONEER

An affiliate auctioneer is an individual who is under direct supervision of an auctioneer and is employed by an auctioneer to deal or engage in offering, negotiating, or attempting to negotiate a listing contract, sale, purchase, or exchange of goods by means or process of auction or sale at auction. The apprentice cannot deal in real property or use the title auctioneer without the word apprentice. (Among many exemptions are volunteers for churches, charitable organizations or political parties, tobacco warehouses, government agencies, and court ordered or sanctioned auctions.)

REQUIREMENTS:
Be at least 18 years of age; honesty, trustworthiness, integrity, good business reputation, and competent; have sponsorship of a registered auctioneer; and satisfy the examination requirement.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
30 hours of rigorous classroom instruction in an auction-related subject approved by the registration authority.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
Examination includes reading, writing, spelling, ethics, licensing, elementary arithmetic, elementary principles of land economics, and Tennessee law relating to bulk sales, auctions, and brokerage.

RENEWAL:
Every two years.

PROFESSIONAL ORGANIZATIONS:
Tennessee Association of Auctioneers
2012 Beach Avenue
Nashville, Tennessee 37204
(615) 292-6619
<…
47-4100000002.agency: Department of Commerce and Insurance · Division of Regulatory Boards · Division of Regulatory Boards

47-4100000025.title: PRE-NEED SALES AGENT REGISTRATION
47-4100000025.description:
PRE-NEED SALES AGENT REGISTRATION

Sell agreements, contracts, or plans at a funeral establishment requiring the payment of money in advance for the final disposition of a dead human body, or for funeral or burial services or burial merchandise, wherein the use of the personal property or the funeral or burial merchandise or the furnishing of professional services by a funeral director or embalmer is not immediately required.

REQUIREMENTS:
Each sales agent at a funeral home must be licensed. If the pre-need funeral contract is funded by an insurance policy, an insurance producer's license is needed.

RENEWAL:
Every two years

47-4100000003.title: PRINCIPAL AUCTIONEER
47-4100000003.description:
AUCTIONEER

An auctioneer is an individual who, for a fee, commission, or any other valuable consideration or expectation of same, engages in offering, negotiating, or attempting to negotiate a listing contract, sale, purchase, or exchange of goods by means or process of auction or sale at auction. The auctioneer can deal in real property only if licensed as a Real Estate Broker or Real Estate Affiliate. (Among many exemptions to registration requirements are volunteers for churches, charitable organizations or political parties, tobacco warehouses, government agencies, and court ordered or sanctioned auctions.)

REQUIREMENTS:
Be at least 18 years of age; honesty, trustworthiness, integrity, good reputation, and competence; and satisfy the experience and examination requirements.

EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENT:
Experience serving as an apprentice auctioneer under the supervision of a licensed full-time auctioneer for a period of two years.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
80 hours of classroom instruction in the fundamentals of auctioneering at an auction school accredited by the commission.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
Examination includes reading, writing, spelling, ethics, licensing, elementary arithmetic, elementary principles of land economics, and Tennessee law relating to bulk sales, auctions, and brokerage. The examination is of a more exact…
47-4100000003.agency: Department of Commerce and Insurance · Division of Regulatory Boards · Division of Regulatory Boards

47-4100000029.title: PUBLIC AUTOMOBILE AUCTIONEER
47-4100000029.description:
PUBLIC AUTOMOBILE AUCTIONEER

A Public Automobile Auctioneer is any individual who, for a fee, commission or any other valuable consideration, or with the intention or expectation of receiving a fee, commission or any other valuable consideration, by the means or process of auction or sale at auction, offers, negotiates or attempts to negotiate a listing contract, sale, purchase or exchange of goods, including motor vehicles.

REQUIREMENTS:
Must complete and submit an application. Must currently be a licensed Auctioneer to apply for a license as a Public Auctioneer License. Must be at least twenty-one (21) years of age. Served as an auctioneer for a period of two (2) years. Complete thirty (30) hours of rigorous classroom instruction in automobile auctioneering approved by the commission.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
High school diploma, some postsecondary training.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
Complete thirty (30) hours of rigorous classroom instruction in automobile auctioneering approved by the commission.

CONTINUING EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
Auctioneers are required to complete 6 hours of continuing education per license cycle (two years). Continuing Education is verified by a Random Audit System therefore you should retain evidence of CE for a minimum of two cycles.

RENEWAL:
Licenses are valid for two (2) years from the…
47-4100000029.agency: Department of Commerce and Insurance · Division of Regulatory Boards · Division of Regulatory Boards

00-67.title: Barge Supervisor
00-67.description: A Barge Supervisor is required to pass an exam, have 3 years of related work experience or an approved degree in engineering or engineering technology, plus at least 168 days of related experience. Specialized training is also required in stability of the mobile offshore drilling unit (ODU), survival at sea, and firefighting. Federal regulations can be found at the web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-67.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-37.title: Chief Mate - Upper Level
00-37.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Mate - Upper Level requires 360 days service as Officer in Charge of a Navigational Watch (OIC) on Any Gross Tons oceangoing steam or motor vessels while licensed as a Second Mate. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. More information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-37.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-34.title: Deck Officers
00-34.description: The navigation of a vessel and management of the deck department is the responsibility of the Deck Officers. Deck officers' licenses are issued by grade (e.g., Master, Chief Mate, Second Mate, Third Mate, Mate and Operator), any vessel type restrictions (e.g. Uninspected Fishing Industry or Uninspected Passenger vessels), means of propulsion (Steam, Motor, Sail or Auxiliary Sail), vessel tonnage (from not more than 5 to any gross register tons), and route (e.g., Inland, Great Lakes, Near Coastal or Oceans). Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-34.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-40.title: Master - Lower Level
00-40.description: Obtaining a United States Coast Guard license as a Master - Lower Level requires a specified amount of qualifying service based on details such as vessel size and area of operation (ocean, near coastal, Great Lakes, or inland). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Detailed information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-40.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-36.title: Master - Upper Level
00-36.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Master - Upper Level requires 360 days service as Chief Mate on ocean Any Gross Tons steam or motor vessels; or 180 days as Chief Mate plus 360 days as Officer in Charge of a Navigational Watch (OIC). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Detailed information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-36.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-66.title: Offshore Installation Manager - OIM
00-66.description: An Offshore Installation Manager (OIM) requires passing an exam and four years of related work experience or an approved degree in engineering or engineering technology and at least 168 days of related work experience. Specialized training in rig stability, oil well control or operation, firefighting and survival at sea are required. OIMs apply for an OIM Unrestricted License or one of four specialized licenses: OIM Surface Units on Location, OIM Surface Units Underway, OIM Bottom Bearing Units Underway, and OIM Bottom-Bearing Units on Location. Federal regulations can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SECTION=470&YEAR=1999&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-66.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-44.title: Pilot (Ship)
00-44.description: A license or endorsement as a Pilot is route-specific and requires experience navigating the body of water specified. A written exam and physical exam are also required. Further information on Pilot requirements can be found on the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/CFR-2002-title46-vol1/CFR-2002-title46-vol1-part10.
00-44.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-69.title: Radar Observer
00-69.description: The Radar Observer certificate is issued by the United States Coast Guard to licensed deck officers. It requires specialized training and examination in radar navigation and is issued for 5 years. Further information can be found in the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10.305) at web site http://frwebgate4.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/waisgate.cgi?WAISdocID=50176913269+4+2+0&WAISaction=retrieve and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-69.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-39.title: Third Mate - Upper Level
00-39.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Third Mate - Upper Level requires 1080 days service in the deck department of ocean steam or motor vessels with 6 months as Able Seaman (AB); or graduate from an approved marine academy; or completion of an approved 3 year apprentice mate training program; or 360 days as Master on ocean steam or motor vessels greater than 200 GT while licensed as a Master 1600 Gross Tons. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. More information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-39.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-68.title: Ballast Control Operator
00-68.description: A United States Coast Guard Ballast Control Operator is required to pass an exam and to have 1 year related experience, including at least 28 days as a trainee under a licensed Ballast Control Operator or a degree in engineering or engineering technology and at least 28 days as a trainee. Specialized training is also required in stability of the mobile offshore drilling unit (ODU), survival at sea, and firefighting. Federal regulations can be found at the web site http://frwebgate2.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/waisgate.cgi?WAISdocID=051618583+1+0+0&WAISaction=retrieve, http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-68.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-46.title: Chief Engineer
00-46.description: To be licensed by the United States Coast Guard as a Chief Engineer, the applicant must complete 360 days of service as a First Assistant Engineer; or while holding a First Assistant Engineer license, complete 360 days of service as follows: a minimum of 180 days of service as a First Assistant Engineer plus a minimum of 360 days as a Second or Third Assistant Engineer, Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-46.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-51.title: Chief Engineer (Limited - Near Coastal)
00-51.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Engineer (Limited - Near Coastal) include 1,440 days at sea, with 360 days as a Licensed Engineer & 720 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-51.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-50.title: Chief Engineer (Limited - Oceans)
00-50.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Engineer (Limited - Oceans), include 1,800 days at sea, with 720 days as a Licensed Engineer & 900 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-50.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-53.title: Designated Duty Engineer
00-53.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Designated Duty Engineer include specified service time at sea, with experience as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED) on a vessel of specified horsepower. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-53.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-45.title: Engineering Officers
00-45.description: The propulsion plant of a vessel and management of the engineering department is the responsibility of the Engineering Officers. Engineering officers' licenses are issued by grade (e.g., Chief Engineer, First Assistant Engineer, Second Assistant Engineer, Third Assistant Engineer, Assistant Engineer and Designated Duty Engineer), any vessel type restrictions (e.g. Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels or Uninspected Passenger vessels), means of propulsion (Steam or Motor), horsepower (from 1,000 to any horsepower), and route (e.g., Near Coastal or Oceans). License limitations for deck and engineering officers, including tonnage and horsepower, are based on the type of experience of each applicant and the passing of applicable written examinations. Each license has separate general, service and examination requirements. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-45.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

47-2900000046.title: SPEECH LANGUAGE PATHOLOGIST
47-2900000046.description:
SPEECH LANGUAGE PATHOLOGIST

Applies non-medical procedures for measurement, testing, assessment, prediction, consultation or instruction in relation to development disorders of speech, voice or language or oral, pharyngeal and laryngeal sensorimotor competencies.

REQUIREMENTS:
Be at least 18 years of age, of good moral character, and satisfy education and examination requirements.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
A Master's Degree in Speech Pathology from an accredited institution.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
ASHA certified or has taken the Praxis examination in Speech Pathology with a minimum score of 600 or 162, depending on the version taken; administered by Education Testing Service, Princeton, New Jersey 08541.

CONTINUING EDUCATION:
A minimum of 10 hours per year of approved coursework.

RENEWAL REQUIREMENTS:
Every two years contingent on satisfying continuing education requirements.

PROFESSIONAL ORGANIZATIONS:
Tennessee Association of Audiologists and Speech Pathologists (TAASLP)
P.O. Box 331307
Nashville, TN 37203
(615) 254-3687

Rockville, MD 20850

47-2900000046.agency: Department of Health · Division of Health Related Boards · Division of Health Related Boards

47-2700000013.title: BOXING RING OFFICIAL
47-2700000013.description:
BOXING RING OFFICIAL

Acts as a judge, referee, or timekeepers at a professional boxing or sparring contest.

CERTIFICATION REQUIREMENTS:
Ring Officials are required to pay a licensing fee of $75 for referees, $50 for judges, $0 for physicians, $100 for announcers, and $50 for timekeepers. An additional $50 fee is required for application. Two photographs must be submitted with licensing paperwork. Licensing requires that the last five years of experience is provided.
47-2700000013.agency: Department of Commerce and Insurance · Division of Regulatory Boards · Division of Regulatory Boards

47-1700000005.title: LAND SURVEYOR
47-1700000005.description:
LAND SURVEYOR

Land Surveyor means a person who is engaged in the practice of land surveying.

Practice of land surveying means any service of work, the adequate performance of which involves the application of special knowledge of the principles of mathematics, the related physical and applied sciences and the relevant requirements of law for adequate evidence to the act of measuring and locating lines, angles, elevations, natural and man-made features in the air, on the surface of the earth, within underground workings and on the beds of bodies of water for the purpose of determining areas and volumes, for the monumenting of property boundaries and for the platting and layout of lands and subdivisions of land, including the topography, drainage, alignment and grades of streets, and for the preparation and perpetuation of maps, records, plats, field notes, records and property descriptions that represent these surveys.

REQUIREMENTS: You are required to submit the following with your Professional Land-Surveyor-in-Training (PLSIT) application:
1. A $25 application licensure fee
2. Proof of Education: A copy of your high school diploma or GED certificate; or a copy of an associate's degree transcript along with a completed course reporting form; or a copy of a bachelor's degree transcript along with a completed course reporting form.
3. Proof of 4 ye…
47-1700000005.agency: Department of Commerce and Insurance · Division of Regulatory Boards · Division of Regulatory Boards

00-64.title: Enrolled Agent - EA
00-64.description: Requirements to become an enrolled agent of the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) are one of the following (1) pass an exam; or (2) document 5 years of relevant experience as an employee for the IRS. Continuing professional education hours every three-year cycle is required for renewal of the credential. Further information can be found at the IRS web site: http://www.irs.gov/taxpros/agents/index.html.
00-64.agency: Internal Revenue Service · Enrolled Practitioner Program Unit

00-79.title: Aircraft Dispatcher
00-79.description: An Aircraft Dispatcher certificate requires that the individual has work experience as an aircraft dispatcher or related occupation such as pilot. Training in aircraft dispatching and passing written and practical tests are also required. This certificate is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked. Detailed information can be found on the web site http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.51-65.70, and http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ

47-5300000001.title: COMMERCIAL DRIVER
47-5300000001.description:
COMMERCIAL DRIVER

Drive multiunit vehicles, single unit vehicles carrying hazardous materials, vehicles carrying more than 15 passengers, or drive school buses. Licenses are classed as A, B, C, or D, each encompassing all classes that follow them alphabetically. The class required depends on the type and weight of the vehicle and trailers if applicable. Endorsements are required for driving tankers carrying 1000 gallons or more, carrying hazardous materials, double or triple units, passenger units, or school buses. Endorsements are required for driving vehicles that use air breaks. (The Class D license is the ordinary driver's license.)

REQUIREMENTS:
Applicants for class A, B, or C licenses must have a Department of Transportation Medical Card, be at least 20-40 in both eyes, and pass examinations. Applicants must be at least 21 years of age to obtain unrestricted licenses or license endorsements. An applicant can qualify for a class B license, restricted to interstate, driving at age 18 or a class A license, restricted to interstate driving, at age 19.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS
: Visual examination, test on knowledge, and skills test in vehicle appropriate to class, are required. An additional written and skill test are required for endorsement authorizing driving vehicles with air brakes.
47-5300000001.agency: Department of Safety · Division of Driver License Issuance

47-2900000057.title: CERTIFIED ANIMAL CHEMICAL CAPTURE TECHNICIAN
47-2900000057.description:
CERTIFIED ANIMAL CHEMICAL CAPTURE TECHNICIAN

An Animal Chemical Capture Technician is an individual employed by a certified governmental animal control agency who is certified by the Board to perform the chemical capture of dogs or cats. The Bureau of Health, Licensure and Regulation of the Veterinary Medical Examiners serves as certifying regulating board.

REQUIREMENTS (general)
1. A completed application;
2. A passport size picture that is signed by the applicant;
3. Required application fee and initial certification fee;
4. The results of a criminal background check to be sent from the vendor directly to the Board office.
Completion of the application before a notary. And Proof of employment of a full-time licensed veterinarian on staff at the agency who will provide direct supervision of the technician operations.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Proof of having successfully completed initial marksmanship training for use of the tranquilizer gun in chemical capture taught by an instructor skilled in using the tranquilizer gun; and proof of having successfully completed a sixteen (16) hour chemical immobilization certification course within twenty-four (24) months of applying for certification. The chemical immobilization certification course must be approved by the Board as provided in T.C.A.  63-12-144(b) and cannot have been taken before…
47-2900000057.agency: Department of Health · Division of Health Related Boards · Division of Health Related Boards

47-2900000006.title: CERTIFIED ANIMAL EUTHANASIA TECHNICIAN
47-2900000006.description:
CERTIFIED ANIMAL EUTHANASIA TECHNICIAN
A person employed by a certified animal control agency who is authorized by the Board of Veterinary Medical Examiners to humanely euthanize animals by administering those drugs approved by the Board.

REQUIREMENTS:
Certificate of completion from a Board-approved course on animal euthanasia.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
None.

CONTINUING EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
None.
47-2900000006.agency: Department of Health · Division of Health Related Boards · Division of Health Related Boards

47-2900000004.title: VETERINARY MEDICAL TECHNICIAN
47-2900000004.description:
VETERINARY MEDICAL TECHNICIAN

A veterinary technician performs procedures that are assigned or delegated to the technician by the supervising veterinarian and do not involve diagnosing, prescribing, or performing surgical procedures. The technician leads or transports animals from its quarters to the treatment room, lifts them to the table, applies restraints or holds them for treatment, sterilizes instruments and equipment using germicides and autoclave, administers anesthetics and medications, and provides prescribed nursing care under the responsible supervision of a licenses veterinarian. Other duties: prepares specified ingredients for foods; feeds, bathes, and brushes animals; cleans hospital rooms and animal quarters; and receives clients or does other office tasks.

REQUIREMENTS:
Graduate from a veterinary technology program approved by the American Veterinary Medicine Association; Successfully complete the examination requirements; Provide proof of good moral character.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
Veterinary Technician National Examination (VTNE).

CONTINUING EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
Obtain twelve (12) hours of continuing education each calendar year. Licensee must retain independent documentation of attendance and completion of all continuing education courses for a period of four (4) years from the end of the calendar year in…
47-2900000004.agency: Department of Health · Division of Health Related Boards · Division of Health Related Boards

47-2900000047.title: VETERINARIAN
47-2900000047.description:
VETERINARIAN

A licensed veterinarian is a person who is validly and currenly licensed to practice veterinary medicine. The practice of veterinary medicine means to diagnose, treat, correct, change, alleviate, or prevent animal disease, illness, pain, deformity, defect, injury, or other physical, dental or mental conditions by any method or mode.

REQUIREMENTS:
Be of good physical/mental health, good moral character, U.S. or Canadian citizen, or legally entitled to reside in the U.S., and satisfy education and examination requirements.

EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Graduate and received a doctorate degree from a school or college of veterinary medicine approved by the Board.

EXAMINATION REQUIREMENTS:
North American Veterinary Licensing Exam (NAVLE).

RENEWAL:
Contingent on satisfying continuing education requirements.

CONTINUTING EDUCATION REQUIREMENTS:
Obtain twenty (20) hours of continuing education each calendar year.

PROFESSIONAL ORGANIZATIONS:
Tennessee Veterinary Medical Associatio
P.O. Box 803
Fayetteville, TN 37334
(931) 438-0070
47-2900000047.agency: Department of Health · Division of Health Related Boards · Division of Health Related Boards

47-5100000001.title: BIOLOGICAL/NATURAL WASTEWATER SYSTEM OPERATOR
47-5100000001.description:
BIOLOGICAL/NATURAL WASTEWATER SYSTEM OPERATOR

Person qualified to control the manipulation of equipment and thereby determine the quality of the effluent from a wastewater treatment plant that is classified as biological/natural. A plant in that classification uses natural biological treatment as the predominant means of treatment, including stabilization ponds, intermittent sand-filters, spray irrigation, constructed wetlands, aerated lagoons, and overland flow systems.

PROSPECTIVE:
Certification is required for persons in direct charge of a wastewater treatment plant classified as a biological/natural system.

REQUIREMENTS:
Must have a high school education or equivalent, have twelve months of operating experience in a wastewater system classified as a biological/natural system, and meet the examination requirement.

CONTINUING EDUCATION:
Within each 3-year period each certified operator must satisfactorily complete a conference, training course, or school approved by the Board.

EXAMINATIONS:
Examination is written (except for accommodations made for disability). It may contain matching, multiple choice, true-false, discussion, and short answer questions and may contain problems. 70% is required to pass.
47-5100000001.agency: Water and Wastewater Certification Program · Fleming Training Center

47-5100000005.title: SMALL WATER SYSTEM OPERATOR
47-5100000005.description:
SMALL WATER SYSTEM OPERATOR

Person qualified to control the manipulation of equipment and thereby determine the quality and quantity of the water supplied by a water distribution system that is classified as a small water system.

PROSPECTIVE:
Certification is required for persons in direct charge of small water systems.

REQUIREMENTS:
An applicant must have a high school education and work in a water system classified as a small water system for at least three months and must meet the examination requirements.

EXAMINATIONS:
Examinations are written (except accommodations made for disability). They may contain matching, multiple choice, true-false, discussion, and short answer questions and may contain problems. 70% is required to pass.
47-5100000005.agency: Water and Wastewater Certification Program · Fleming Training Center

47-5100000006.title: WASTEWATER COLLECTION SYSTEM OPERATOR GRADE I
47-5100000006.description:
WASTEWATER COLLECTION SYSTEM OPERATOR GRADE

Person who is qualified to control the manipulation of equipment and thereby determine the integrity of a system classified as Grade I for the collection and transmission of wastewater to a treatment plant.

PROSPECTIVE:
Certification is required for persons in direct charge of wastewater collection systems of Grade I.

REQUIREMENTS:
An applicant must have a high school education or equivalent, twelve months operating experience in a wastewater collection system, and meet examination requirements. A maximum of three months of college classwork or related training can be substituted for the same amount of experience.
